thread.title: Close Update: Wall Street Crushed By Earnings, Rising Bond Yields as Dow Plunges 660 Points

title: Close Update: Wall Street Crushed By Earnings, Rising Bond Yields as Dow Plunges 660 Points
text:
Close Update: Wall Street Crushed By Earnings, Rising Bond Yields as Dow Plunges 660 Points February 02, 2018, 04:30:04 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo 
Stocks plunged on Friday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average sinking more than 660 points in the worst decline in almost two years on widespread losses after disappointing earnings for its blue-chip members and worries about interest rates. 
The rout on Wall Street accelerated to cap a wobbly week for markets as a hawkish Federal Reserve statement coupled with strong labor data to raise concerns about climbing rates, sparking selling in bonds that pushed yields on US Treasuries higher. 
Earnings weighed on Friday, with Apple ( AAPL ), ExxonMobil ( XOM ) and Merck ( MRK ) all retreating amid mixed quarterly reports and guidance from the Dow components. All of the blue chips slid, sending the Dow to the lowest close since Jan. 10. 
"Optimism has fled the stock markets," analysts from Canadian bank Desjardins said in a note. The CBOE Volatility index, or VIX, jumped 29% to the highest since late 2016. On the week, the Dow dropped 4.2%, the S&P 500 lost 3.9% and the Nasdaq slid 3.5%. 
Selling pressure accelerated through Friday's session after the Labor Department reported an increase of 200,000 in non-farm payrolls and 0.3% gain in average hourly earnings. The data drove the 10-year yield to a four-year high of 2.85% and the Dow below 26,000. The last time the Dow posted a decline of more than 600 points was in June 2016. 
On the S&P 500, all 11 sectors sank, with energy shedding the most, sliding 4.1% by the close as oil prices retreated and amid a 5.1% loss for Exxon and an 5.6% decline in Chevron. Information technology dropped 3% as Apple ( AAPL ) shed 4.3% and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) lost 4.8% and 5.3%. 
Politics emerged as another worry, with less than a week to go before lawmakers need to approve another measure to continue funding US government operations. Also on Friday afternoon, a controversial, previously classified memo was released by Republican lawmakers about allegations of misconduct by Federal Bureau of Investigation officials. 
Here's where the markets stood by the close:
